newsitem.title: UK: Mercury wins contracts up to 100 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Mercury wins contracts up to 100 mln stg.

text.p: Britain's Mercury Communications, one of the four firms forming Cable & Wireless Communications, said on Tuesday that it had been awarded two telecom systems contracts from the government.
"The deals are worth five million stg in the first year and up to 100 million over five years," Mercury said in a statement.
The contracts are in regard to Government Telecommunications Services (GTS) and Government Telecommunications Mobile (GTM) and would cover voice, data and mobile services.
The contracts have been awarded by the Central Computer and Telecommunications Agency.

"Through these contract Cable & Wireless Communications will help put in place part of the infrastructure necessary to deliver government services in ways that are more efficient, more convenient and easier to use," Robert Fisher, managing director of C&W Communications corporate markets said.
